title: Ignoring repeated ones
statement: For the specified bit transducer, let $q$ be a state such that reading a one leaves the state unchanged and $q$ is not the output state. For every natural number $k$ and finite bit string $r$, starting in $q$ and reading $k$ consecutive ones followed by $r$ produces the same output as reading $r$ from $q$.
hypotheses_covered: Reading one in state $q$ leaves the state unchanged.
The state $q$ is not the output state.
The repetition count $k$ is a natural number.
The suffix $r$ is a finite bit string.
